question: How do I turn on Stellar's built-in fully-private, shielded-by-default transaction mode for all my payments?

golden.answer:
A grounded answer consults the current official Stellar documentation, directly answers the question with source-supported content, and dates any version-, provider-, or availability-sensitive claim. As of 2026-11-02, the verified sources supported this observed answer:

Stellar has no network-wide switch, CLI flag, or account setting that makes all payments shielded by default. Ordinary Stellar transactions and standard asset/token activity are public by default. Privacy requires an explicit application or token protocol: current official material describes Stellar Private Payments, an unaudited Testnet developer preview of a privacy pool, and Confidential Tokens, whose audited OpenZeppelin v0.8.0 contracts SDF called ready to deploy on Mainnet on 2026-10-22. By design, Confidential Tokens hide balances and transfer amounts but leave sender/receiver addresses public; the current verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge proofs, so OpenZeppelin does not guarantee that privacy yet. Stellar Private Payments has different visibility boundaries. BLS12-381 (CAP-0059/P22) and BN254/Poseidon (CAP-0074/0075/P25) are cryptographic primitives, not a global privacy mode. State each product's network, audit, and field-visibility status; do not fabricate enablement steps.

The dated example is illustrative: a later grounded answer should report what the same source basis supports at its own observation time while preserving the stable distinctions above.
keyFacts: Presents specific current or dated source evidence, not unsupported memory.
Makes the as-of date visible for every changeable roster, status, version, or measurement.
Stellar has no global shielded-by-default transaction mode.
Scopes public transparency to ordinary and default Stellar activity.
avoid: Do NOT invent an enablement command or claim Stellar is shielded by default.
Do NOT say all application-layer balances/amounts must remain visible or imply unaudited Testnet previews are audited Mainnet products.
Do NOT present version-, provider-, interface-, or availability-sensitive observations as timeless; date the changeable part without weakening stable protocol or historical facts.
golden.notes:
GT-25 CORRECTION 2026-07-10: no global privacy toggle exists, but current optional applications can hide defined fields. Grade ordinary/default transparency plus explicit product network, audit, and visibility status; BN254/Poseidon are live P25 primitives, not a turnkey mode.
GT-25 independently confirmed by processes 3268/3273.
REFRESH 2026-11-02: Confidential Tokens v0.8.0 contracts are audited and called Mainnet-ready, but the verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge proofs. An answer that reports this limit does not fire the visibility avoid. The designated auditor can decrypt amounts by design. Do not credit a claim that a public observer can recover every amount from proofs or chain data; the sources say only that further leakage is not ruled out.
